Okay so this is a browser extension idea, um, for Chrome mainly. I do a lot of competitive research and I'm constantly on competitor pricing pages, and they change their prices and plans all the time, silently. I want an extension where, when I'm on any page, I can hit a button and select a region of the page, like the pricing table, and the extension snapshots just that region, the text content of it. And then it checks that page on some schedule when the browser is open, and if the text in that region changed, it shows me a diff, like old versus new, highlighted. Kind of like, um, like Git diffs but for a chunk of a webpage. I want the history kept locally, I really don't want to run a server for this or send people's browsing anywhere, that's a privacy thing and also I just don't want backend costs. It should export a change history as CSV for when I write reports. The tricky bits I guess are pages that load stuff late, like the pricing table pops in after a second, and pages that want you logged in. It's just me building it, evenings, and honestly if the Chrome store review is a pain I want to keep permissions minimal so it doesn't get stuck in review forever.
